summary: Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution
description:
### Summary

PHP can access freed memory when collecting the arguments of a method handled by `__call()` or `__callStatic()` for a backtrace. On PHP 8.5 and later, an unauthenticated attacker may be able to trigger this through a crafted request that causes a fatal error while the application enters such a method. Successful exploitation can execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the PHP

summary: Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown
description:
### Summary

As part of CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), PHP 8.5.12 fixes a generic use-after-free of the `last_fatal_error_backtrace` global by clearing it during executor shutdown. Further scenarios have been discovered in which a fatal diagnostic during later shutdown work repopulates the global. The request heap is then released, and an early diagnostic in a subsequent request handled
